message.content:
To terminate **Visual Studio Code** (`code.exe`) from the command line on Windows, you can use the built‑in `taskkill` utility.

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

### What each part does

| Argument | Meaning |
|----------|---------|
| `/IM`    | Specifies the image name (process executable). |
| `code.exe` | The exact name of the VS Code process. |
| `/F`     | Forces termination – the process will be killed immediately. |

> **Tip:** If you only want to kill a specific instance (e.g., one with a particular window title), first list all running processes:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

This shows the PID(s) of each `code.exe`. Then you can target a single PID:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <pid_number> /F
```

---

#### Quick checklist

1. Open an elevated Command Prompt (Run as Administrator) if you encounter permission errors.
2. Run `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` to stop all VS Code windows.
3. Verify with `tasklist | findstr code.exe` – there should be no entries left.

That’s all you need to force‑close VS Code from the command line!
